newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania to sell stake in airline, railway.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania to sell stake in airline, railway.

text.p: Lithuania expects to sell a minority stake in state-run Lithuanian Airlines in 1998 and aim for the privatisation of the railways in 18 months time, the country's deputy transport minister said on Tuesday.

"The (transport) ministry decided to look for a serious strategic partner and investor for Lithuanian Airlines during 1997 and to start the privatisation at the earliest in 1998," Deputy Transport Minister Algirdas Sakalys told Reuters.
Sakalys said 51 percent of the shares in Lithuanian Airlines will remain in state hands after the sale to a strategic investor. Its current share capital is 76.5 million litas.
The views of the transport ministry on the privatisation of Lithuanian Airlines and the railway company will be handed to the government for its backing this week.
If the ministry carries through its plan, it will mean that all Baltic republic airlines have foreign partners.
Estonian Air, the former state-owned carrier of Estonia, is part-owned by Maersk while Latvian airline, Air Baltic, has Scandinavian Airlines as investor.
The privatisation of Lithuanian railways will also be up for discussion as soon as its current restructuring is completed in a year and a half, Sakalys added.
The railway restructuring will separate the railway operators and carriers from the infrastructure, which will not be sold off. This was the model followed by Britain when it sold off its railways.
The restructuring of Lithuanian railways, whose share capital is 1.2 billion litas, is being carried out with the assistance of Irish CIE Consult and Danish DanRail.
